policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 2:1 reads 'they were all together in one place'. 'together' renders the adverb ὁμοῦ of the base; the alternative ὁμοθυμαδὸν is 'with one accord', which the ASV does not have here.

καὶ ἐκάθισεν and ἐκάθισέν τε differ only in the connective's form and position; ASV 'and it sat upon each one of them' renders either. The verse's only note is an alternative_rendering about 'parting asunder' and does not touch this unit.
πάντες and ἅπαντες are the same word with and without the strengthened prefix; ASV 'they were all filled' renders either and no note bears on it.
Pure word order between ἀποφθέγγεσθαι and αὐτοῖς; ASV 'as the Spirit gave them utterance' fixes English order independently of the Greek sequence.
ASV 'dwelling at Jerusalem' uses a single locative 'at' that renders either ἐν or the equivalent εἰς of place-where; nothing in the English or a note distinguishes the prepositions.

The number of the verb is not visible in English: ASV 'every man heard them speaking' takes its singular from the subject εἷς ἕκαστος, so both the plural ἤκουον (ad sensum) and the singular ἤκουσεν yield this wording.

ASV 2:7 reads 'And they were all amazed and marvelled'. The 'all' of the main clause has no other source in the verse (the later 'all these that speak' renders the separate πάντες/ἅπαντες of unit v010), so the ASV renders the reading that adds πάντες.

ASV 2:7 has a bare 'saying, Behold, are not all these...' with no 'one to another'; the ASV renders πρὸς ἀλλήλους explicitly where it stands (cf. 2:12 'saying one to another'), so its absence here shows the shorter reading.
Οὐχ, Οὐχὶ and Οὐκ are forms of the same negative before the question; ASV 'are not all these' renders any of them.
πάντες and ἅπαντες are the same word; ASV 'all these that speak' renders either.
Active διηπόρουν and middle διηποροῦντο carry the same sense; ASV 'and were perplexed' renders either voice.
ASV 'What meaneth this?' is the conventional English for both the indicative θέλει and the potential ἄν θέλοι; the English gives the potential no separate marker, so it does not distinguish them.
διαχλευάζοντες and χλευάζοντες differ only by the prefix and both mean 'mocking', which is exactly what ASV 2:13 has.
The unit is the presence of the article with the proper name; English 'But Peter' shows no article either way.
πάντες and ἅπαντες are the same word; ASV 'all ye that dwell at Jerusalem' renders either.
Dative ἐνυπνίοις and accusative ἐνύπνια are alternative constructions of the same cognate object; ASV 'shall dream dreams' renders either. The verse's only note is the Joel citation.
πρὶν ἢ and πρὶν with the infinitive are equivalent; ASV 'Before the day of the Lord come' renders either.
Presence or absence of the article with ἡμέραν is not visible in ASV 'the day of the Lord', whose 'the' is required English for a definite phrase either way.
ἐὰν and ἄν are interchangeable in the relative clause ὃς ἄν/ἐὰν ἐπικαλέσηται; ASV 'whosoever shall call' renders either.
Pure word order of ἀποδεδειγμένον and ἀπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ; ASV 'a man approved of God unto you' follows English order and cannot distinguish the sequences. The verse's note is a greek_gloss on 'powers'.

ASV 'even as ye yourselves know' uses 'even as' as its standing rendering of καθὼς alone, and the same phrase would serve for καθὼς καί; the emphatic 'yourselves' renders αὐτοί, not the added καί, so the English does not settle the addition.

ASV 2:23 has only two finite verbs for the hearers, 'did crucify and slay', with nothing answering to λαβόντες ('ye have taken', as in versions following the longer reading); the participle is unrepresented, so the ASV renders the base.
ASV 2:23 reads 'by the hand of lawless men', singular, matching χειρός; the alternative χειρῶν is plural ('hands'). The verse's note concerns the rendering of ἀνόμων only.
Pure word order of μου with ἡ καρδία; ASV 'my heart was glad' renders either sequence.
εἰς ᾅδην and εἰς ᾅδου are alternative forms of the same phrase; ASV 'unto Hades' renders either.

ASV 2:30 runs straight from 'that of the fruit of his loins' to 'he would set one upon his throne', with nothing answering to τὸ κατὰ σάρκα ἀναστήσειν τὸν χριστόν ('according to the flesh he would raise up the Christ'); the ASV renders the shorter reading.

ἐπὶ with accusative τὸν θρόνον and with genitive τοῦ θρόνου are both 'upon his throne' after a verb of sitting; ASV does not distinguish the case, and its note offers only an English alternative ('one should sit').

ASV 2:31 reads 'that neither was he left unto Hades, nor did his flesh see corruption' — a correlative 'neither...nor' answering οὔτε, and no subject 'his soul' in the first member; the alternative reads οὐ κατελείφθη ἡ ψυχὴ αὐτοῦ, which the English does not show.
ᾅδην, ᾅδου and ᾍδου are alternative forms and capitalisations of the same word; ASV 'unto Hades' renders any of them.
ASV 'nor did his flesh see corruption' renders οὔτε and οὐδὲ alike; English 'nor' is the standard rendering of both after a preceding negative.
Pure word order within 'the promise of the Holy Spirit'; ASV's phrase renders πνεύματος τοῦ ἁγίου and ἁγίου πνεύματος identically. The verse's note is an alternative rendering of the preposition.
ASV 2:33 reads 'which ye see and hear', without the 'now' that renders the added νῦν; the ASV represents that adverb where it stands, so its absence shows the base reading.
ASV 'which ye see and hear' has no 'both' or other rendering of the καί that the alternative places with ὑμεῖς (ὑμεῖς καὶ βλέπετε, 'ye both see'); only the single 'and' joining the two verbs appears.
The unit is the presence of the article with κύριος; ASV 'The Lord said unto my Lord' supplies English 'The' either way.
Pure word order of αὐτόν within 'him both Lord and Christ'; ASV's clause renders either sequence.
Pure word order of ἐποίησεν and ὁ θεός; ASV 'that God hath made him' follows English order and does not distinguish them.
Accusative τὴν καρδίαν and dative τῇ καρδίᾳ are alternative constructions after κατενύγησαν; ASV 'were pricked in their heart' renders either case.
ASV 'what shall we do?' serves for both the deliberative subjunctive ποιήσωμεν and the future ποιήσομεν; English 'shall we' does not separate them.

ASV 2:38 reads 'And Peter said unto them, Repent ye' — one verb of speaking before the quotation, which fits the base and its punctuation variant (with the verb of saying understood) as well as ἔφη πρὸς αὐτούς. It excludes the reading with parenthetical φησίν inside the quotation, which the ASV would render 'saith he' after 'Repent ye'.
ASV 'in the name of Jesus Christ' is the standing rendering of both ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι and ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι in this formula; the English preposition does not distinguish them.
The unit is the article with ἁμαρτιῶν; ASV 'the remission of your sins' shows no article on 'sins' either way, its definiteness coming from 'your'.
ASV 2:38 reads 'unto the remission of your sins'; the possessive 'your' renders ὑμῶν, which the alternative omits.
ASV 2:40 reads 'he testified, and exhorted them'; the object 'them' renders αὐτούς, which the alternative omits.
ASV 2:41 reads 'They then that received his word were baptized', with no 'gladly' answering to the added ἀσμένως; the verse's note offers only 'Or, having received' for the participle.
ASV 'in that day' renders both ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐκείνῃ and the bare dative of time; English requires 'in' either way.

ASV 2:42 reads 'in the apostles’ teaching and fellowship, in the breaking of bread and the prayers': no 'and' stands between 'fellowship' and 'in the breaking', where the added καί would be rendered. The note is an alternative rendering of κοινωνίᾳ itself.

ASV 'And fear came upon every soul' uses a simple past that renders both the imperfect Ἐγίνετο and the aorist Ἐγένετο. The verse's textual_variant note concerns an addition ('in Jerusalem; and great fear was upon all'), not this unit.
τε and δὲ are both rendered by the connective 'and' that opens ASV 2:43; the English does not distinguish them, and the verse's note is about an addition elsewhere in the verse.
ASV 'all that believed' renders both the present πιστεύοντες and the aorist πιστεύσαντες; the English participial phrase carries no aspect marker.

ASV 2:44 reads 'And all that believed were together, and had all things common': the finite 'were' renders ἦσαν and the 'and' before 'had' renders the καί, both of which the shorter reading lacks (it leaves ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό without them).

ASV 2:47 reads 'the Lord added to them day by day those that were saved', and its greek_gloss note on that phrase reads 'Greek together' — an explicit gloss of ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό. The alternative τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ would give 'to the church', which the ASV does not have.
